stem: A male client taking spironolactone develops new breast enlargement and tenderness. Which adverse effect should the nurse recognize?
rationale: Spironolactone can cause gynecomastia, and its labeling also lists breast and nipple pain among reproductive adverse reactions. Therefore B best matches new breast enlargement and tenderness. Hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and hypotension are also recognized spironolactone risks, but they do not describe the breast finding in the stem.
educational_objective: Recognize gynecomastia as a labeled adverse effect of spironolactone when a male client develops breast enlargement or tenderness.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.1 Hyperkalemia, §5.2 Hypotension and Worsening Renal Function, §5.3 Electrolyte and Metabolic Abnormalities, §5.4 Gynecomastia; Adverse Reactions §6 — Reproductive
source_claim_supported: Spironolactone can cause gynecomastia; breast and nipple pain are reported reproductive adverse reactions. Hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and hypotension are separate labeled risks.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: Educate client about medications; Evaluate client response to medication; Review pertinent data prior to medication administration
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — spironolactone adverse effects
correction_summary: Rebuilt the alternatives so all four are genuine labeled spironolactone adverse effects rather than mixing drug effects with unsupported diagnostic claims. Changed the keyed letter from A to B while preserving gynecomastia as the correct clinical concept, removed unsupported 'must discuss with prescriber' wording, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
